newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain strike set to disrupt public sector.
newsitem.headline: Spain strike set to disrupt public sector.

text.p: A Spanish public sector strike of up to two million workers was set to disrupt postal services, courts, television transmissions, hospitals and schools on Wednesday, trade unions said.
Large demonstrations were also planned in regional capitals to protest against a freeze on 1997 salaries of civil servants which the government claims is vital to meet its budget goals.
Police in Madrid have put anti-riot officers on alert.
Unions said they would call two million civil servants to a 24-hour strike and were confident of a significant turnout.
The conservative government sparked mass protests in July when it announced it would freeze public sector salaries in 1997 aimed at getting Spain in shape for European Monetary Union.
The government has secured basic emergency services and some minimum services in schools, post offices, airports and prisons.
Spanish airport authority AENA said on Tuesday it expected little impact on air travel to and from Spain with near normal staffing levels.
Unions rejected a last-ditch attempt by the government to avert the strike with a promise to raise salaries in 1998 and 1999 to compensate for the freeze.
But the government did not not back down on its planned freeze which it claims is vital to its entry into the single European currency.

The unions, led by the Workers' Commission (CCOO) and the General Workers' Union (UGT), say the freeze violates a deal with the previous socialist administration which guaranteed wages would rise in line with inflation in 1997.
